item.title: In Haiti, Salvadoran troops destroy the house of the 400 Mawozo gang’s leader
item.description:
El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, on Tuesday claimed the assault on the gang’s headquarters in Croix-des-Bouquets, where its leader was absent. American diplomats complain that El Salvador is acting without co-ordinating with the UN-backed force.

At around 2.30am on Sunday 8 November a drone unit of the Haitian police, backed by Salvadoran soldiers and helicopters, destroyed the house of Wilson Joseph, leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, in Croix-des-Bouquets near Port-au-Prince, described as his headquarters. El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, who had vowed to raze the house, claimed the operation on Tuesday; it reportedly left about 20 dead according to the Miami Herald, a toll AFP could not confirm, and Wilson Joseph was absent, according to the Salvadoran press. Haiti’s prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, praised El Salvador, but American diplomats complain that the 2,000 or so Salvadoran soldiers, most of them outside the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force, are not co-ordinating with it, according to Axios.

item.title: Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang reaches out to the state as Salvadoran troops close in
item.description:
Wilson Joseph’s gang says it has contacted the national disarmament commission and wants UN mediation. The prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, has announced the killing of a gang leader in Cité Soleil.

On Friday 6 November the 400 Mawozo gang, led by Wilson Joseph, told the Associated Press that it had contacted Haiti’s national commission for disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration in the name of “peace” and “national reconciliation”. Accused by the UN and human-rights groups of rape, murder and kidnapping, which it denies, the gang fears an offensive by the more than 2,000 Salvadoran soldiers deployed in recent weeks, and El Salvador’s president, Nayib Bukele, has promised to destroy its leader’s house. The same day the prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, announced the death of a gang leader in Cité Soleil, identified by police as the head of the Boston gang, while the disarmament commission says it is following the government’s road map.
